items.title: V2.2.0 Large Authentication Response from AMF crashes AUSF
items.description:
I am referring the issue here just in case it hasn't been noticed yet.

https://gitlab.eurecom.fr/oai/cn5g/oai-cn5g-ausf/-/issues/6

This issue is critical and easy to re produce. AMF doesn't crash but AUSF does. It can cause denial of service.

items.title: AMF V2.2.0 returns successful response before NGSetup has been established
items.description:
**Bug Description:**

OpenAirInterface v2.2.0 accepts `NGReset` , `RANConfigurationUpdate` and returns success before NGSetup is established. Protocol specifies NGSetup must be established first.

**Steps to reproduce:**

Launch AMF. Configuration used

[config.yaml](/uploads/f0e9daeb6edfaf461cd2c05e91f051be/config.yaml)

Send these NGAP messages (packet is in hex stream) sequentially

NGReset

00 14 00 1A 00 00 02 00 0F 40 02 00 00 00 58 00 0D 40 01 68 C9 A8 A8 DA 3E C0 FF FF FF FF

**Expected behavior:**

AMF should reject the message or shouldn't process the message.

**Environment:**

* OpenAirInterface Version: v2.2.0
* OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Server
* Deployment: Docker

PCAP:

[oai_reset.pcap](/uploads/28c3db602c28493cb770320d0a3fc2bc/oai_reset.pcap)

items.title: AMF V2.2.0: Non-cleartext IE is being accepted at InitialUEMessage
items.description:
**Bug Description:**

OpenAirInterface v2.2.0 accepts InitialUEMessage with Non-cleartext IE (Capability GMM). It is a violation of 3GPP 24.501 specification, allowing potential UE capability leakage and profiling.

**Steps to reproduce:**

Launch AMF. Configuration used

[config.yaml](/uploads/f0e9daeb6edfaf461cd2c05e91f051be/config.yaml)

Send these NGAP messages (packet is in hex stream) sequentially

NGSetup

**00 15 00 38 00 00 06 00 1b 00 08 00 00 f1 10 00 00 06 6c 00 52 40 05 01 00 52 41 4e 00 66 00 0d 00 00 00 00 07 00 00 f1 10 00 00 00 08 00 15 40 01 20 00 93 40 01 00 00 cc 40 01 00**

InitialUEMessage (UE Security- Capability GMM added)

00 0f 40 45 00 00 05 00 55 00 02 00 **02** 00 26 00 1b 1a 7e 00 41 79 00 0d 01 00 f1 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 10 2e 02 80 f0 10 01 00 00 79 00 0f 40 00 f1 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 f1 10 00 00 07 00 5a 40 01 18 00 70 40 01 00

**Expected behavior:**

AMF should reject the registration request during initial Registration Request as it shouldn't proceed with UE GMM Capability sent as a clear text

**Environment:**

* OpenAirInterface Version: v2.2.0
* OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Server
* Deployment: Docker

PCAP:

[oai_cleartext.pcap](/uploads/df69384eb58f07e51cd92da76d9b6700/oai_cleartext.pcap)

items.title: AMF V2.2.0 Integrity 5G-IA0 is accepted bypassing integrity check
items.description:
**Bug Description:**

OpenAirInterface v2.2.0 accepts Security Mode Accept without any integrity protection. Configuration has supported integrity NIA1 and NIA2. But if an UE sends initial registration request with only security capability IA0, OpenAirInterface accepts and proceeds. This downgrade security context can lead to the possibility of replay attack.

**Steps to reproduce:**

Launch AMF. Configuration used

[config.yaml](/uploads/f0e9daeb6edfaf461cd2c05e91f051be/config.yaml)

Send these NGAP messages (packet is in hex stream) sequentially

NGSetup

**00 15 00 38 00 00 06 00 1b 00 08 00 00 f1 10 00 00 06 6c 00 52 40 05 01 00 52 41 4e 00 66 00 0d 00 00 00 00 07 00 00 f1 10 00 00 00 08 00 15 40 01 20 00 93 40 01 00 00 cc 40 01 00**

InitialUEMessage (UE Security- IA0 supported only)

00 0f 40 45 00 00 05 00 55 00 02 00 01 00 26 00 1b 1a 7e 00 41 79 00 0d 01 00 f1 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 10 2e 02 80 80 10 01 00 00 79 00 0f 40 00 f1 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 f1 10 00 00 07 00 5a 40 01 18 00 70 40 01 00

UplinkNASTransport (Authentication Response)

00 2e 40 3c 00 00 04 00 0a 00 02 00 0a 00 55 00 02 00 01 00 26 00 16 15 7e 00 57 2d 10 0a 39 9e 7c af f8 ab 86 e9 fa 79 80 dc 57 7a 36 00 79 40 0f 40 00 f1 10 00 00 00 00 00 00 f1 10 00 00 07

UplinkNASTransport (Security Mode Command) with MAC field = 0

**Expected behavior:**

AMF should reject the registration request during initial Registration Request as it shouldn't proceed with UE Capability with no integrity IA0 as per specification. It should reject immediately. And AMF configuration also suggests that it doesn't support IA0. No further state progression shouldn't happen.

**Environment:**

* OpenAirInterface Version: v2.2.0
* OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Server
* Deployment: Docker

items.title: AMF V2.2.0 Incorrect State Transition - Authentication bypass
items.description:
**Bug Description:**

We observed this behavior in OpenAirInterface V2.2.0, Out of sequence messages are causing incorrect state transition during UE registration procedure. This allows authentication to be bypassed completely. If a SecurityCompleteMessage is sent after InitialUERegistration, a registration reject is received followed by a registration accept!

Launch AMF using this configuration: 

[config.yaml](/uploads/2435de8fccfb71e652536c6f9ee39bcf/config.yaml)

items.title: Authentication Reject not being sent after multiple synch failure
items.description:
Issue on behalf of the University of Hong Kong (team members: Xue Zhang, Jiatao Cheng, Wei Yi, and Yi Chen)

During our analysis of the AMF authentication procedure in the OAI CN5G core network, 

We identified a behavior that appears to be non-compliant with 3GPP TS 24.501 §5.4.1.3.7. Specifically, after receiving two consecutive AUTHENTICATION FAILURE messages with 5GMM cause # 21 (“synch failure”), the AMF continues to retransmit the AUTHENTICATION REQUEST instead of terminating the procedure with an AUTHENTICATION REJECT, as specified in the standard.

We have prepared a detailed technical report describing the issue, along with supporting materials to facilitate reproduction and analysis. The attachments include:

1. A detailed issue report
2. PCAP traces demonstrating the observed behavior
3. The modified UERANSIM source files used to reproduce the issue
4. Ready-to-use UERANSIM gNB and UE configuration files for connecting to the OAI CN5G core network, provided to simplify reproduction

We hope this information will be helpful to the OAI community. Please feel free to let us know if further details, clarification, or additional experiments are needed.

items.title: UE De-registration fails silently
items.description:
Hi,

Using current HEAD (aka: `v2.1.0`) in `oai-cn5g-fed`, with the minimal scenario `docker-compose-mini-nonrf.yaml`, an AsKey low-power in-door gNB, and a CrossCall mobile in 5G.

Everything works like a charm, except for de-registration: when the mobile is put to plane mode, despite the mobile cleanly releasing, the AMF periodic status in the log shows it stays `5GMM-REGISTERED` *forever*.

A bit of digging shows the following exchanges between the gNB and AMF.

The salient part is the `InitialUEMessage, Deregistration request (UE originating)` which is **not** followed by anything.

```shell
... [infinite loop of HEARTBEAT/HEARTBEAT_ACK]
534 2025-08-03 13:47:55,918297 gNB → AMF SCTP 100 HEARTBEAT
535 2025-08-03 13:47:55,918379 AMF → gNB SCTP 100 HEARTBEAT_ACK
536 2025-08-03 13:47:58,721009 gNB → AMF NGAP/NAS-5GS 128 UplinkNASTransport, UL NAS transport, PDU session release request (Regular deactivation)
537 2025-08-03 13:47:58,723970 AMF → gNB NGAP/NAS-5GS 136 PDUSessionResourceReleaseCommand, DL NAS transport, PDU session release command (Regular deactivation)
538 2025-08-03 13:47:58,760906 gNB → AMF NGAP/NAS-5GS 144 UplinkNASTransport, UL NAS transport, PDU session release complete
539 2025-08-03 13:47:58,760967 gNB → AMF NGAP 92 PDUSessionResourceReleaseResponse
540 2025-08-03 13:47:58,761041 gNB → AMF NGAP 92 UEContextReleaseRequest
541 2025-08-03 13:47:58,761043 AMF → gNB SCTP 64 SACK
542 2025-08-03 13:47:58,761988 AMF → gNB NGAP 104 UEContextReleaseCommand
543 2025-08-03 13:47:58,872546 gNB → AMF NGAP 120 UEContextReleaseComplete
544 2025-08-03 13:47:59,073849 AMF → gNB SCTP 64 SACK
545 2025-08-03 13:47:59,223428 gNB → AMF NGAP/NAS-5GS 136 InitialUEMessage, Deregistration request (UE originating)
546 2025-08-03 13:47:59,425810 AMF → gNB SCTP 64 SACK
547 2025-08-03 13:48:04,878310 gNB → AMF SCTP 100 HEARTBEAT
548 2025-08-03 13:48:04,878401 AMF → gNB SCTP 100 HEARTBEAT_ACK
560 2025-08-03 13:48:11,534310 gNB → AMF SCTP 100 HEARTBEAT
561 2025-08-03 13:48:11,534403 AMF → gNB SCTP 100 HEARTBEAT_ACK
... [infinite loop of HEARTBEAT/HEARTBEAT_ACK]
```

Correlating this with the AMF logs shows:

```shell
 oai-amf     | 2025-08-03T11:47:59.224758838Z [2025-08-03 13:47:59.223] [amf_app] [debug] Received NAS_SIG_ESTAB_REQ
 ...
 oai-amf     | 2025-08-03T11:47:59.224863487Z [2025-08-03 13:47:59.224] [amf_n1] [debug] Received InitialUeMessage De-registration Request message, handling...
```

.. then nothing **ever** from `[amf_n1]`, as though the asynchronous "handling" was simply aborted, silently.

Looking into the code gives the explanation:  these log messages show that `nas_data_ind.is_nas_signalling_estab_req==true` :

```c
   /* amf_n1.cpp*/
    void amf_n1::handle_itti_message(itti_uplink_nas_data_ind& nas_data_ind) {
      ...
      if (nas_data_ind.is_nas_signalling_estab_req) {
        Logger::amf_n1().debug("Received NAS Signalling Establishment request...");
        nas_signalling_establishment_request_handle(
            type, nc, nas_data_ind.ran_ue_ngap_id, nas_data_ind.amf_ue_ngap_id,
            decoded_plain_msg, snn, ulCount);
      } else {
        Logger::amf_n1().debug("Received Uplink NAS message...");
        uplink_nas_msg_handle(
            nas_data_ind.ran_ue_ngap_id, nas_data_ind.amf_ue_ngap_id,
            decoded_plain_msg, plmn);
      }
```

Indeed, the `nas_signalling_establishment_request_handle()` function then does nearly nothing about the de-registration, it merely logs it:

```c
   case kDeregistrationRequestUeOriginating: {
      Logger::amf_n1().debug(
          "Received InitialUeMessage De-registration Request message, "
          "handling...");
    } break;
```

while, in the "normal" case (`is_nas_signalling_estab_req==false`), the alternative function `uplink_nas_msg_handle()` does a more thorough job about de-registration:

```c
    case kDeregistrationRequestUeOriginating: {
      Logger::amf_n1().debug(
          "Received De-registration Request message, handling...");
      ue_initiate_de_registration_handle(
          ran_ue_ngap_id, amf_ue_ngap_id, plain_msg);
    } break;
```

So, why in the first place is this de-registration considered as "signalling establishment", in other words a "fresh context" ? A hint may be provided by the logs about "No context found ... create a new one":

```shell
    oai-amf     | 2025-08-03T11:47:59.224765228Z [2025-08-03 13:47:59.223] [amf_app] [warning] No existing UE context associated with key app_ue_ranid_27:amfid_8
    oai-amf     | 2025-08-03T11:47:59.224772354Z [2025-08-03 13:47:59.223] [amf_app] [debug] No existing UE Context, Create a new one with ran_amf_id app_ue_ranid_27:amfid_8
```

Could it be a race condition, with the context being freed "too early" after the ContextRelease procedure, inducing De-Registration to be considered as an invalid beginning for a signalling session, and dropped ?

items.title: AMF sends Initial Context Setup Request when UE context is setup in RAN
items.description:
See [oai-gnb-l2-trace.pcap](/uploads/e873870b459a450a0a23f424fe964ed7/oai-gnb-l2-trace.pcap):

In packet 63693, there is an UL NAS transport for a UE that is already known (RAN-UE-NGAP-ID=2, AMF-UE-NGAP-ID=12). It contains registration request. The core answers with an initial context setup request in packet 63694, but that UE is already known. As of gNB tag `2024.w41`, the gNB asserts.

The question is: _is the core allowed to send the initial context setup request when the UE context is already set up?_ 38.413 is not clear to me in this case.

In oai/openairinterface5g!3038, the gNB might accept a initial context setup request sent for an existing UE again, under the condition that the security algorithms/keys do _not_ change. In fact, in this case, the gNB just ignores those keys. If they change, I am not sure how to handle this, as we cannot set up AS Security, since 38.331 says that a RRC SecurityModeCommand cannot come when there is a DRB (which might be the case), and does not mention if a second SecurityModeCommand is actually allowed.

- the UE deletes a security context, it needs to indicate that to AMF by using NAS key set identifier IE and set the value to no key is available (section `9.11.3.32 NAS key set identifier` @ 3GPP TS 24.501 version 16.14.0 ) in the Registration Request message, so that AMF can trigger a new authentication procedure

items.title: Configuration: No validation
items.description:
Most of the AMF configuration values are not validated, i.e. the `validate` value is not overriden and also the regex validators of string values and the intervals of int values are not set accordingly.

We should implement this similar to SMF, so that the user is not confused when there are mistakes during PDU session establishment because of an illegal configuration. These kind of scenarios are really hard to debug, which is why the validation is so useful. Also, it may prevent security issues.

items.title: Configuration: SD should be an int
items.description:
The `SD` value in AMF SNSSAI configuration is a string, but it should be an int. `yaml-cpp` is able to correctly read also a hex value here, so we can safely use an int type here. 

Also, there is no validation of this value. 

In any case, I am working on unifying the slicing configuration over all NFs including AMF, so we don't have to fix this in AMF right now.

items.title: Configuration: We should have a default GUAMI
items.description:
Currently, when configuring the AMF and the user does not provide anything in `served_guami_list`, there is nothing configured. I suspect it will lead to the case that AMF is effectively unusable (or maybe there is some handling of this somewhere).

To make it easier for us and the user, we should have one default GUAMI (similar to DNN and subscription config in SMF).

items.title: Configuration: What should we do with AMF Name
items.description: The `amf_name` configuration is used to generate the AMF profile towards NRF. Is this really necessary? We could also just use the `host` value. In SMF this value is hardcoded to `OAI-SMF`. In any case, we should align the ways how to we create the profile.

items.title: Huge length for Initial Context Setup Request from AMF
items.description:
When testing the OAI Core with RAN+UE Emulator, it seems the AMF is sending more bytes for Initial Context Setup Request than expected. E.g. usual length of this message is 165 or < 200 bytes in normal cases including NAS PDU (Registration Accept) in it. However, AMF here seems to send more bytes, when seen on pcap of Wireshark too. Due to this at the RAN, receives additional bytes and tries to decode the additional bytes too. Attached pcap is one such have 1320 bytes of payload in NGAP. [ICSR-More-length-issue.pcapng](/uploads/77a2f3dcb0daf2d742d49bafd2f7c283/ICSR-More-length-issue.pcapng)

It seems when using  msg->encode2Buffer(buffer, BUFFER_SIZE_2048); on the AMF side, those additional bytes are getting appended than the required. If  msg->encode2NewBuffer(buffer, encoded_size); is used instead, the problem is not seen and only the required bytes are present as per the length of the respective NGAP message. Kindly review and fix.

items.title: GUTI format
items.description: According to 3GPP, 5G-GUTI is defined as <MCC><MNC><AMF Region ID><AMF Set ID><AMF Pointer><5G-TMSI> in which 5G-TMSI is a integer (with 32 bits length). The string representation of TMSI should be 32 bits (4 bytes) accordingly e.g., '0001' is the string representation of 0x00000001 (1).

items.title: AMF is at 100% CPU after gNB disconnect
items.description:
The CPU utilization is at 100% for the AMF (in docker container) once a gNB disconnects for the first time.

Using `gdb`, I saw that `sctp::sctp_server::sctp_receiver_thread()` loops over the open sockets. I wonder whether there is an unhandled event, due to the fact that inside the loop there is `if (FD_ISSET())` without a corresponding `else`. The other option could be a non-blocking socket.
